title: "FRRouting Cheat Sheet"

# FRRouting Cheat Sheet

FRR runs on Linux; host interfaces and addresses are visible through `ip`, while routing daemons are managed through `vtysh`. Daemons must be enabled in the image or lab configuration. Replace the node and interfaces with those in your topology.

## Connect and inspect

```sh
docker exec -it clab-LAB-r-frr vtysh
docker exec clab-LAB-r-frr ip -br address
docker exec clab-LAB-r-frr ip route show
```

At the `vtysh` prompt:

```text
show running-config
show interface
show ip route
show ipv6 route
show ip ospf neighbor
show bgp summary
show bgp ipv4 unicast
show bgp ipv4 unicast 203.0.113.0/24
```

## Configure and verify a static route

```text
configure terminal
ip route 192.0.2.0/24 10.1.12.2
end
show ip route 192.0.2.0/24
```

Remove it with `no ip route 192.0.2.0/24 10.1.12.2` in configuration mode. A route requires a reachable next hop. FRR configuration persistence depends on the container image and its mounted configuration; `write memory` writes the configured FRR files, but lab recreation can replace them. Save changes in the lab's source configuration.

## Troubleshoot

Compare FRR's route with Linux `ip route get 192.0.2.1`; check interfaces, neighbor state, and captures with `tcpdump -ni eth1`. BGP and OSPF show commands require their corresponding daemons and configuration.
